articles.title: Belfast court injuncts decision to allow Orange Order march down Garvaghy Road
articles.summary: Andy Burnham calls for calm as fears of unrest grow after request for countermarch in mainly nationalist area A controversial loyalist parade down a nationalist street in Portadown has been…

blocks.text: A controversial loyalist parade down a nationalist street in Portadown has been temporarily injuncted after a high court judge urged all sides to “step back from the abyss” and take responsible decisions for “the sake of everyone in Northern Ireland”.
The ruling was made amid rising fears that a parade could unleash fresh sectarian violence.

After a five-hour hearing at a special sitting of the high court, Justice Smyth issued an order temporarily suspending the parade, which was due to take place at 8am on Sunday, until a judicial review application can be fully heard.
She has also suspended the determination by the Parades Commission on Friday that the event could take place, albeit with restrictions on numbers.
However tensions remain with an appeal against her decision by loyalists to be heard at a second special hearing on Saturday night.
Smyth arrived at her conclusions after several attempts to coax the parties, the Loyalist Orange Order and the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition, to reach a voluntary agreement.

After it was clear that was not possible, she said: “The level of mistrust between residents and Portadown Loyalist Lodge cannot be overstated. Neither side accepts any of the reassurances of the other.”
The march down Garvaghy Road has been banned for 28 years due to widespread sectarian violence in 1998 outside Drumcree church.
“It is also clear to me that this particular long-running dispute has the potential to escalate within Northern Ireland,” she said.
The court was sitting on Saturday following a last-minute legal challenge by the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition.
Smyth urged parties to reach a voluntary agreement to delay the march, given few had time to digest the reasoning behind the Commission’s decision.
It was important “to reach an agreement for the sake of everyone in Northern Ireland, not just for your sake” to have the issues “properly aired” so that “everybody knows they’ve had a fair hearing”.
“Be big enough to step back from the abyss,” she told the parties in court.
This followed a high court ruling quashing the restrictions of the annual parade route.

blocks.caption: People gathered outside Belfast high court on Saturday 26 September awaiting the decision by Justice Smyth over the planned Garvaghy Road march. Photograph: Mark Marlow/PA

blocks.text: The Portadown loyalist Orange Lodge was not represented at the hearing. But after a request from the judge for its view through the individual who had sought permission for the parade, the lodge made it clear it would not agree to suspending the procession.

Fears of clashes increased on Saturday after a request to the Commission for permission for a countermarch, a protest that, it was estimated, could be attended by up to 5,000 people, the court heard. That was later revised to 300.

On Friday night, the British prime minister, Andy Burnham, appealed to leaders to “work calmly” through the weekend while the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, called for “cool heads”, saying Northern Ireland had “withstood many moments of sharp disagreement over the years” and must do so again.

Before her ruling, Smyth asked the parties in court, including the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) and the Parades Commission, to “consider carefully the very important issues to our society” raised in this case, and the importance that they were dealt with properly given the “importance of this case to community relations”.
She also noted that the issues of judicial review were of “such fundamental importance” that it could be unwise to hold a full hearing without all the facts.

Democratic Unionist MP Carla Lockhart insisted nationalist residents on the road had “nothing to fear” from the march on Sunday, but Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald described the decision as “utterly reckless”.

The Parades Commission has placed a number of restrictions on the procession, including an 8am start and limiting the number of participants to 35 people, but not placing any restrictions on the route.

articles.title: Nor'easter storm brings coastal flooding, as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
articles.summary: Tens of millions of people from Maine to Virginia are in the path of the powerful storm.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Surf City, New Jersey, was among coastal communities flooded

Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm this weekend, which has already brought coastal flooding, power outages, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.

Peaking on Saturday, the so-called nor'easter will "bring dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds, and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.
States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, the latter of which is already facing a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.
Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Residents on kayaks in a Beach Haven West, New Jersey, neighbourhood

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Residents on kayaks in a Beach Haven West, New Jersey, neighbourhood
The nor'easter is already causing widespread power outages. Nearly 150,000 households have so far lost electricity, according to poweroutageus.
The Federal Aviation Administration recommended flyers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 1,100 flights have been delayed and another 400 grounded, according to FlightAware.
Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal inundations. Streets and homes were flooded on Saturday in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan.
"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert, and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Flooding in New Jersey

blocks.text: Flooding in New Jersey

blocks.caption: Image caption, Flights have been cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport

blocks.text: Flights have been cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport
NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."
In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power outages.
"Don't travel if you don't have to," Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."
In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs from Sunday afternoon game to next Friday.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Waves pound the coast in Massachusetts

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Waves pound the coast in Massachusetts
A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.
Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead.
Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston-area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.

articles.title: Third person arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, as police say hanging was staged
articles.summary: Eric Clark, 45, charged with murder as autopsy concludes Fortune was dead days before body discovered in tree A third person has been arrested in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune in Mississippi…

blocks.text: A third person has been arrested in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune in Mississippi’s capital city, while investigators said they had determined the scene where her body was found hanging had been staged.
Eric Clark, 45, surrendered to authorities on Friday and was charged with murder, according to the Jackson police department (JPD). Clark was scheduled to make a court appearance on Monday.
Police disclosed Friday that an autopsy investigation concluded “the scene and the hanging were staged”.
Authorities did not release additional information about the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s killing or why investigators believe the scene was faked.
Clark’s arrest comes after two other men, Earnest Lloyd Jr and Jarques Ratliff, were charged with murder in connection with Fortune’s death.
The case leading to the arrests of Clark, Lloyd Jr and Ratliff had drawn national attention because of the severity of Fortune’s killing and Mississippi’s history of racist violence and lynchings.
Clark, Lloyd Jr, Ratliff are Black, as was Fortune.

“The Jackson police department’s robbery-homicide division will continue its investigation until all individuals believed to be involved are held accountable for their actions in connection with Ms Fortune’s death,” a news release shared with multiple news outlets states.
Fortune, a mother of four, was discovered on 3 August hanging from a tree behind a vacant home on the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in the western part of Jackson.
Investigators have said Fortune was not killed at the location where her body was found.

JPD detective Samuel Dukes previously described Fortune’s hanging in court as “staged”, saying investigators believe she was killed somewhere else before her body was placed in a hanging position in the tree on Road of Remembrance. He added investigators determined Fortune had been dead for two to three days before her body was discovered.
Police have released few details about the events leading to Fortune’s death. Detectives have interviewed as many as 15 people, according to the police news release.

Local TV news station WLBT reported an alleged physical altercation between Lloyd, 25, and Fortune that occurred shortly before her death. Police accused Lloyd of using a black cable cord to hang Fortune, according to WLBT.
Ratliff and Lloyd have both reportedly pleaded not guilty. Each has been denied bond.
Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, has said she was certain her daughter would not have killed herself.

articles.title: Palace tells Sara Duterte: Defend with proof, not fallacies
articles.summary: Malacañang hit back at Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday, telling her to learn to recognize the flaws and fallacies in her arguments after she accused the Marcos administration of being…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 1:15am

Malacañang hit back at Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday, telling her to recognize the flaws and fallacies in her arguments after she accused the Marcos administration of being “desperate” to bring her down.

In a Viber message to reporters, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro urged Duterte to address the accusations against her with evidence rather than relying on fallacies in defending herself.
“Maturuan sana ang Bise Presidente na matuto siyang sumagot nang may ebidensiya sa mga inaakusa sa kanya bago magturo ng iba,” Castro said in a Viber message to reporters.
(May the Vice President learn to answer the accusations against her with evidence before pointing fingers at others.)

Castro was responding to Duterte's accusation, which she made while denying allegations that she knew and received money from Rodolfo Gracioso Jr., a former policeman who served as a security officer for then-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The Vice President dismissed the claims as another media stunt and a desperate move by the administration to bring her down and breathe life into the “faltering impeachment case” against her.
“The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical,” Duterte said.
Castro said Duterte should familiarize herself with logical fallacies and improve how she responds to the allegations.
“Alamin niya ang definition ng red herring at ad hominem fallacies para malaman niya ang kamalian niya sa pakikipag-argumento,” she said.
(May she learn the definition of red herring and ad hominem fallacies so she can understand the flaws in her arguments.)

“Uulit-ulitin natin para tumimo sa isipan (We will repeat this again and again so it sticks in her mind): She needs to level up her defending skills so she can appear credible, if only for once,” she added.

In an exclusive interview with GMA News, Gracioso alleged that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte on Velasco's instructions.
Gracioso estimated that he had delivered a total of more than P2 billion to the Vice President.
For his part, Velasco also denied the allegations against him, asserting that they were completely baseless.

“The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested,” said Velasco's spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan, in a statement.
The National Bureau of Investigation said it has begun its probe into Gracioso's claims. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Wisconsin police investigating fraternity for hazing after men found in basement
articles.summary: Pledges found covered in food in heated basement of fraternity house near University of Wisconsin-Madison Police are investigating suspected illegal hazing after about 30 partially clothed young men…

blocks.text: Police are investigating suspected illegal hazing after about 30 partially clothed young men covered in food, condiments and other liquids were found recently in the basement of a fraternity house near the University of Wisconsin-Madison campus.
Madison police said some of the men, whom they described as pledges of a fraternity, had signs of being physically assaulted.

Police went to the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) fraternity house on Wednesday night after receiving an anonymous tip. Two fraternity members, both 20, were arrested on tentative misdemeanor charges of hazing and disorderly conduct, police said. No formal charges had been filed against them as of Friday morning.
The university said it was taking the case seriously and launching its own investigation.
“UW–Madison is fully committed to preventing and addressing hazing and takes all incidents involving our community seriously,” the university said in a Thursday statement.
Any student found to have broken the law or university policy could be subject to sanctions ranging from a written reprimand to expulsion, UW-Madison said.

Police released a photo that shows about two dozen men, all shirtless, in the basement of the fraternity with trash and other debris on the ground. The faces of the people in the photo are blurred out.

Police said the thermostat had been set to 81F, causing hot and humid conditions in the basement, where the walls appeared to be painted black. A majority of people in the basement were 18 years old, police said.

The fraternity’s status as a recognized student organization on the Madison campus was terminated in 2015 for holding events while suspended. It had been suspended in 2013 for hosting a party in which a 17-year-old and another person were taken to detox after being served alcohol at a party hosted by the fraternity, according to university records.
The termination came after a fourth incident involving either events, alcohol or both, the university said.
Since 2016, there were seven additional allegations involving the fraternity related to intramural sports, disrespectful behavior, drinking and hazing, the university said.
Because the fraternity is still recognized by its national organization, it is able to operate as a fraternity chapter unaffiliated with the university, UW-Madison said.

National fraternity spokesperson Jon Pierce said his organization is taking the allegations “very seriously” and will cooperate fully with investigations. Any member found to have participated will be expelled from the fraternity, he said.
“Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for,” Pierce said. “There is no place for it in AEPi. No exceptions. No excuses.”
The fraternity house is located just blocks from the heart of the UW-Madison campus, which is home to about 52,000 students.

Police said their investigation is also ongoing. The university’s office of student conduct and community standards is also investigating in accordance with its nonacademic misconduct process, UW-Madison said.

articles.title: Greek authorities seek answers after six killed in Athens apartment block explosion
articles.summary:
Emergency teams discovered victims after two-storey building in historic Plaka district collapsed ‘in a matter of seconds’

Greek authorities say they are trying to discover what caused a…

blocks.text: Greek authorities say they are trying to discover what caused a two-storey apartment block in the heart of ancient Athens to collapse “in a matter of seconds”, killing six people.
Emergency teams found the victims, including four American tourists, on Saturday, more than 24 hours after an explosion prompted the early morning tragedy in the historic Plaka district.

The fire service said the bodies of three women and three men had been found, but stopped short of identifying them. A Briton and his Greek wife, aged 77 and 78, who lived in a flat on the building’s upper floor, were among those killed, the Guardian was told.

“The bodies have been taken to the morgue where postmortems will be conducted,” the city’s vice-mayor Paris Charlaftis said in a telephone interview from the blast scene. “Our focus now is on the explosion’s cause. What could have happened to bring the building down in a matter of seconds?”

Rescuers had deployed thermal cameras and geophones, used to detect deep subsonic frequencies, in the hope of finding survivors. Earth-moving machines and specially trained search dogs were brought in to move and comb mounds of rubble through the night.

Before the bodies were pulled from the ruins on Saturday, police put the missing at six, saying four were Americans staying in a short-term rental on the building’s first floor. Two brothers and their wives, all four were due to fly to the US on Friday, just hours after the explosion.

blocks.caption: Police have put the missing at six. Photograph: Costas Baltas/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: “When they failed to turn up for the flight they had checked into only a day earlier, that gave us a further lead,” a source said. “It became clearer that they must have been there when the blast occurred.”

The Briton, a talented artist, who lived with his wife on the second floor, was described as being partially disabled by Charlaftis. “He had kinetic issues, and it was thought likely they, too, were in the building [at the time of the blast].”

Nestled around the foot of the fifth-century BC Acropolis, Plaka is especially popular with tourists. The picturesque district draws thousands of visitors daily, with many staying overnight in the hotels and short-term rentals in neoclassical houses and small apartment blocks along its alleyways and narrow streets.
The mayor of Athens, Haris Doukas, who rushed to 15 Lysikratous where the mid-20th century building had once stood, was quick to describe the incident as an “unprecedented disaster”.

At least three people were known to have been injured when the 7.30am explosion occurred, shattering the windows of nearby buildings and scattering debris far and wide. A motorist driving down Lysikratous described how his car was lifted into the air by the sheer force of a blast that some in the neighbourhood likened to an earthquake, others to a bomb. Emergency workers could be seen hastily removing two women on stretchers from a building next door who had been wounded by flying debris.

Speculation is rife that a gas leak triggered the collapse but officials said there were many “cogent theories” at play. Fears of the leak emanating from the first-floor short-term rental was among them.
after newsletter promotion
As part of efforts to address a burgeoning housing crisis, Greece’s centre-right government has sought to ban short-term rentals in Plaka – clamping down on permits and tightening regulations.
On Saturday, as speculation mounted over the cause of the blast, criticism grew over the ability to “properly control” establishments that were often unregulated.

“This awful incident will fuel further debate over who inspects short-term rentals that no one who lives in Plaka wants anyway,” said Giorgos Zafeiriou, an architect who heads the local residents’ committee. “Hotels have chambers that regulate them but who inspects and controls Airbnb and serviced apartments that often may not be up to par?”
Civil protection crews and emergency disaster management teams have been ordered to remain on site until the cause of the explosion is found, officials said.
“It was a huge explosion, so getting to the bottom of it must now be the priority,” added Zafeiriou. “Six people have lost their lives.”

articles.title: ‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference
articles.summary:
Exclusive: UK prime minister says delivering fiscal stability would be ‘crucial’ to be able to fix bigger problems

Andy Burnham has said he can deliver on his promise of radical change for…

blocks.text: Andy Burnham has said he can deliver on his promise of radical change for the country despite severe economic headwinds, telling the Guardian: “There’s always things you can do, it’s just whether you’re prepared to do them.”

The prime minister acknowledged the public finances were “challenging” ahead of next month’s budget but said that delivering fiscal stability would be “crucial”, because only then would the government be able to focus on fixing bigger problems.

A series of global economic shocks, including the Iran conflict, have put the UK economy under intense inflationary pressure and pushed up borrowing costs, leaving the government limited room for manoeuvre.

Ahead of his first Labour conference as prime minister, however, Burnham sought to both reassure voters he was willing to make tough decisions to deliver change, and to show the markets that he could ensure fiscal stability while preparing the groundwork for more substantial change ahead.

Speaking to the Guardian on the eve of his first conference as Labour leader, he said: “The public would have more respect for us if we go and grab something difficult … and say, ‘Right, we’re going to do something here’, rather than constantly playing the political game before fixing the problems.

“It’s challenging, definitely, but there are still things that you can do. Always in politics, there are things that you can do. The question is sometimes: Are you prepared to do them? Yeah, I am prepared to do them.”

When asked about the need for a large fiscal buffer against shocks, he said the key thing was stability, indicating that he understood the need to reassure the markets, but that more radical transformation of the state would follow.

“I do think it is crucial to have stability and to show that there’s a willingness to face up to the reality of some of these difficult things. But actually from that stability, the permission can come to make bigger change that, in the end, could put the country in a stronger position in relation to the public finances,” he said.
“You have to have stability, but you have to do what you can within that. You can’t pursue a major programme of change, which is what I believe the country needs, in a chaotic situation.”

After ruling out holding a snap general election before 2029, Burnham said that he wanted to set out a clear path for how the country could move to a better place – and that he hadn’t been spending his time “sitting politicking and strategising” but instead was focused on fixing problems.
His ambition to give people “a bit more belief that things can improve” across the country, he said, would not come from “endlessly running elections and referendums”.

He denied having had any discussions with his senior team about whether to call an early election. “The speculation in no way matches the internal discussion because there isn’t one,” he said, rejecting claims he did not have a mandate as the public had voted for the Labour party.
However, Burnham acknowledged he was hemmed in on tax and the fiscal rules of Keir Starmer’s manifesto commitments, and suggested he would have done it differently had he been in charge at the time.

“I’ve inherited those positions and, as I say, I think the main thing for me is to focus on the here and now for people, not to be self-serving about ‘oh, what would suit me?’ and playing politics. That’s not where my mind is, and possibly would have framed it different, but we are where we are, you know, and that’s the reality.”

Burnham played down speculation that Labour may give more support for energy bills, with the cap price set to soar from January. “I think people need to remember that measures have already been taken,” he said, referring to VAT on electricity bills being scrapped from next week.

The prime minister also reiterated that while he thought the welfare bill was too high, the will among Labour MPs was “not there for crude cuts” because they would push people into crisis, so a longer term approach to reform was required.

After warning of the risks, as well as the opportunities of artificial intelligence at the UN last week, Burnham admitted to concerns about rogue AI agents attacking state institutions in the UK, after the Australian medicare system was hit.

Burnham addressed the presence of far-right protesters on the streets of Britain, accusing Daniel Thomas, who has led black-clad anti-migrant vigilantes on the streets of some English towns, of “creating fear” but did not go as far as Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, who accused him of being an “outright racist”.

Speaking of Thomas’s masked gangs, he said: “I mean that’s not Britain. That’s not what we want to see in people’s communities. There’s legitimate concerns about issues, and then there is intimidation – and that is intimidation,” he said.
after newsletter promotion

The prime minister also addressed political funding, which has been in the spotlight since Reform UK received two record-breaking £36m donations from cryptocurrency billionaires, saying that – contrary to reports – he would not rule out a domestic donations cap.

“You know I think we do need to continue to have a cross-party discussion about how do we uphold trust in politics? How do we do not give the impression that politics can be bought and that people are, if you like, unduly influenced?”
He was also open to looking at election spending limits, he said, which are now being examined by the Electoral Commission, adding that he has “real concerns” about crypto-fuelled politics.

An emotional Burnham revealed that the death of his father, Roy, last week had made him more determined to deliver. “I’m in this job for what I can do for people, not for what it can do for me … to make the changes that my dad, for instance, long pushed me to make,” he said.
“It’s been a hard thing, if I’m honest, coming into this position in the last three months when I also knew in my heart that I was starting this journey as my dad was ending his.

“Although that’s hard, and I’m not seeking sympathy in saying it, I say it because the coming together of those two things increases my determination to make a difference on the things that I’ve long said I want to fix.”

With political courage expected to be a focus of his speech to Labour’s conference in Liverpool, Burnham said he was willing to be honest with the public about what needed to happen, even if it was difficult to hear.

“I think the public want to see, number one, honesty about things. So not spin or putting things a certain way that’s self-serving. They want honesty, and then they want, I think, difficult but real decisions,” said Burnham.
“Not difficult decisions and making a fetish out of that, but actually grasping nettles and then moving things forward. I don’t think politics has been prepared to do that enough in recent times.”

Burnham criticised previous governments for failing to tackle difficult issues such as social care, housing supply and youth unemployment, saying longer term reform was needed because there were no “easy or quick wins”.

He revealed there would be a new help-to-buy scheme aimed at giving first-time buyers who cannot rely on the “bank of mum and dad” the keys to their own home. It will be funded by reallocating existing budgets, although it is unclear which ones, rather than through extra borrowing.

Burnham also said he wanted to deliver significant progress on social care reform – a manifesto commitment – before the next election. “Who is going to do something to actually make it real? I’m saying to you that I am going to address this directly.”
