articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections
articles.summary:
President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest

Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning…

blocks.text: Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.
The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.

The provisional executive order comes into force immediately but will need congressional approval within 120 days to remain in effect. It prohibits new deposits into accounts and gives users of betting platforms until 5 October to withdraw their funds.

Lula’s government has also drafted a bill to establish criminal offences related to fixed-odds betting – the most common and dominant type of online sports betting – such as promoting them and using personal data to solicit punters.
“I made the decision to take a hard, drastic and necessary measure,” he told journalists in São Paulo. “It’s like cancer, you take out the tumour, or the tumour will kill us.”
Lula had also criticised the betting industry earlier this week at the United Nations general assembly, accusing it of “transforming addiction into profit” and of “destroying homes”.
Polls suggest a ban enjoys widespread support among Brazilians. Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula’s main rival in the upcoming election, accused the current leader of an “electoral measure”.

Brazil’s president has sharply criticised online betting at least since April, when he called for a ban. The public backlash against it grew during the Fifa World Cup when advertisements were ubiquitous and the number of people betting surged.

Betting and gambling are estimated to cost Brazilian society 38.8bn reais (£5.6bn) annually and increases suicide and depression, according to a 2025 study by the nonprofit Institute of Studies for Health Policies.

The country’s central bank estimated last year that Brazilians spend about 30bn reais on bets each month. That figure included spending by beneficiaries of the cash-transfer federal welfare programme Bolsa Familia (family grant), which was blocked from those platforms last year.
Lawmakers, including many from Flávio Bolsonaro’s Liberal party, struck down a Lula order for tax hikes on online betting and virtual casinos in October last year.

Gambling is illegal in Brazil, but the country opened the gates to online betting in 2018 during the presidency of Michel Temer. The phenomenon snowballed under the watch of the former president, Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio Bolsonaro’s father.

In December 2023, Lula signed a law to regulate and tax betting companies for the first time. Months later, his administration blocked more than 2,000 online betting websites that were designated as irregular, including some linked to criminal organisations such as the First Capital Command from São Paulo and the Red Command of Rio de Janeiro. It was part of a national push to regulate the sector.

Lula and members of his administration have spoken about banning online betting as necessary to both close a drain to the country’s economy and to tackle a public health issue, as many Brazilians are addicted and in financial difficulties due to spending their money on these platforms.
Business analysts say that revenues for sports betting, one of the betting models banned on Friday, are estimated at more than $4bn (£3bn) per year in Brazil, one of the biggest markets in the world.
Before Friday’s move, Brazil’s main football clubs sounded the alarm after betting companies reportedly warned that their sponsorships would end immediately if the government banned betting.
They said the move could lead to the end of Brazilian football, a claim mocked by some social media users in the football-mad country.

blocks.text: India and Pakistan traded accusations at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Friday, with Islamabad criticizing India's stance on Kashmir and New Delhi accusing Pakistan of supporting cross-border terrorism.
Addressing the General Assembly, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for "a just and fair resolution of the Kashmir dispute," alleging human rights violations in the region.
Sharif also brought up the military clashes last year between the uneasy neighbors, calling them "external aggression from India under a false pretext."

Pakistan considers Indian missile strikes on May 7 to be the start of the low-level conflict, which ran for less than a week, while India contends that the strikes were retaliation for an attack in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir in April last year.
He added that India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis and accused New Delhi of "weaponizing" water.

India rejected Sharif's remarks. First Secretary at India's UN mission Petal Gahlot accused Pakistan of "terrorism, deceit and duplicity" and said Islamabad's support for cross-border terrorism would have consequences.
Gahlot also criticized Pakistan's military establishment and its treatment of minorities, while reiterating India's position that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of the country.

articles.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
articles.summary: An emergency has been declared across the capital of Thailand as days of heavy rain leave the city inundated.

blocks.text: Disaster declared as heavy rain sparks Bangkok flooding
A flood emergency disaster has been declared across Bangkok after 48 hours of heavy rain left roads in the Thai capital submerged.
People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city's network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors.

Thunderstorms are common in Thailand at this time of year but extreme weather in recent days has inundated Bangkok's drainage system, causing traffic chaos on roads that are already famously congested.
The rain is expected to continue into Sunday, raising fears that more canals could burst their banks.
Image source, Getty Images
Canals across the Thai capital have burst their banks, leaving roads under water
Somkid Pheuk-ngam, a 67-year-old who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok, told the AFP news agency: "The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now."
She said water levels in the city appeared to be worse than in 2011, when Bangkok was impacted by nationwide flooding.
Hundreds were killed across Thailand then in an extreme weather event that lasted for three months. So far, no casualties have been reported in Bangkok from this latest flooding.
The Thai Meteorological Service has forecast more heavy rain through the week, though the area of low pressure causing the downpours of recent days is expected to move towards central Thailand.

blocks.caption: People holding umbrellas and walking down a narrow flooded street in Bangkok

blocks.text: All 50 of Bangkok's districts have been declared emergency zones.
Chadchart Sittipunt, the city's governor, said the east of the city had been hardest hit, AFP reported.

He continued: "The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full... The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled."

articles.title: Velasco camp: Reports of illegal activities have 'no basis'
articles.summary: The camp of Lord Allan Velasco on Saturday issued a statement on what they called "fabricated attacks' on the former House Speaker, saying the allegations against him have "no basis."

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 2:35pm
The camp of Lord Allan Velasco on Saturday issued a statement on what they called "fabricated attacks" on the former House Speaker, saying the allegations against him have "no basis."

"The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested," said Velascos' spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.
Velasco's camp also called the accusations against the former speaker as "inconsistent."

"The "one-size-fits-all" narration by this individual seems to be designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events, that is, the Covid-19 pandemic, Atty.Velasco's period of service as speaker, other details, and even basic common sense," added Velascos' spokesperson.

On Friday, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., who claim to have served as a security officer for Velasco, said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte as ordered by the former speaker.
Velasco's camp, however, urges the public to be "more circumspect" about the allegations.

"We respectfully urge everyone to be more circumspect in appreciating this news report while we evaluate and determine the accountability of the individual and the publisher under the law," said Atty. Ilagan.
Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday also denied Gracioso's claim.
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.

"This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case. The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," she said.
Gracioso estimated that he had delivered a total of more than P2 billion to Sara Duterte.
He also said he also brought money to then-President Rodrigo Duterte at Malacañang between 2018 and 2022, and delivered a suitcase containing P100 million to Pulong Duterte.
Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida confirmed in a message to GMA News that the Department of Justice had received Gracioso’s affidavit and was evaluating it.
GMA News has sought comments through phone calls and messages from Pulong Duterte and Rodrigo Duterte since Thursday, but they have yet to give any.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said it is investigating Gracioso's claims. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: DMW chief Cacdac orders 'comprehensive reintegration' support for Mary Jane Veloso
articles.summary: Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac has ordered the provision of full reintegration assistance for former overseas Filipino worker (OFW) Mary Jane Veloso following her grant of absolute pardon…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 2:35pm

Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac has ordered the provision of full reintegration assistance for former overseas Filipino worker (OFW) Mary Jane Veloso following her grant of absolute pardon and subsequent freedom from jail.
In a statement, the DMW said Cacdac has ordered a support team to coordinate with Veloso's family in Nueva Ecija to facilitate her "comprehensive reintegration."
The team is tasked to "lay the groundwork for immediate family- and community-level interventions" that would allow Veloso's long-term productivity and self-sufficiency.
"Our instructions are clear: the DMW must stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Mary Jane, her children, and her parents as they rebuild their lives," Cacdac said.
Cacdac said her "tailored reintegration program" involves direct discussions her family and local stakeholders.
The DMW issued the statement hours after President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. said Friday that he has already signed the order for Veloso's absolute pardon.

On the same day of the President's announcement, Veloso was released from the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City, turning the page on the 16-year chapter of her life spent behind bars on drug charges.
The DMW said it is working with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) to ensure that Veloso's transition to her new life is sustainable.
This involves linking her "ventures directly to local cooperatives and municipal economic opportunities in Nueva Ecija," with the goal that this would foster community participation.
Veloso languished on death row in Indonesia following her arrest in April 2010 at the Adisutjipto International Airport in Yogjakarta for alleged possession of heroin.
Veloso and her supporters have long insisted that she was exploited as drug mule and was actually the victim in the case.
She was sentenced her to death in October 2010, but a strong appeal from the late President Benigno Simeon "Noynoy" Aquino III paved the way for the commutation of her punishment in 2015.
In December 2024, Indonesian authorities agreed to transfer custody over Veloso to the Philippines. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: OpenAI tools post user images from ChatGPT online
articles.summary: OpenAI said it found 53 cases in which user-uploaded image links on ChatGPT were shared with third-party websites. The company said it had removed most of these links.

image.caption: OpenAI said it had removed most of the leaked content and was working to remove the restImage: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI on Friday acknowledged that its AI tools had posted images users provided to ChatGPT on online sites, without the company's knowledge, in yet another example of AI agents operating outside of their confines.
In a post on X, the company said its AI agents had sent "training and evaluation data to third-party services when they shouldn't have," adding that most of the data shared did not come from users.
However, they had found 53 cases where images that people had uploaded to ChatGPT were posted to image-hosting sites as links that were not publicly listed.
"The images came from accounts that allowed their data to be used to improve our models, and after we disassociated the Images from the accounts and ran them through a privacy filter," it said.
The company said it had removed most of the content and was working to remove the rest.
Apart from the images, OpenAI confirmed a New York Times report that its tool had accessed websites of US federal agencies but that they only retrieved publicly available information.
Tech giant OpenAI heads for Wall Street
Rising fear of rogue AI

The latest disclosure comes amid heightened global concerns about AI systems escaping human control and hacking into external websites, as well as industry calls for a slowdown on AI development — a move which OpenAI said it supports.
Friday's post also clarified that the cases of unauthorized sharing occurred before a fresh round of safeguards were implemented over a month ago.

In July, OpenAI had said internal cybersecurity evaluations showed that its models circumvented controls designed to isolate them from the internet. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Friday said it was "still the most severe event we've seen."

"We are continuing to review agent activity in research and evaluation runs, working backward month by month starting from the Hugging Face incident," OpenAI said in a safety blog post on Friday, adding that it would "provide further updates" in time.
How US, China could end the AI race
Investigation finds OpenAI agents attempting hacks

AI evaluator and research lab Transluce on Friday said that it also found that AI agents, appearing to originate from OpenAI, attempted a rudimentary hack on the US Department of Education website for the department's civil rights office. The agents did not succeed, according to the independent investigation.

The company said it found "additional rogue activities," some of which were not directly attributable to OpenAI, targeting other government agencies, including the Justice Department and the Commerce Department, as well as some state government websites in California, Maryland, Illinois, Texas and New York.

articles.title: No ghost projects in Taguig, DPWH chief Vince Dizon tells Alan Cayetano
articles.summary: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon said that based on his agency's ongoing investigation, it has yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 1:47pm

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon said that based on his agency's ongoing investigation, it has yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig City.
During the Senate hearing Friday on the DPWH budget for 2027, Senator Alan Peter Cayetano asked Dizon if the department has identified a ghost project in the former's political bailiwick of Taguig.
"Wala po. Sa aming imbestigasyon, wala po," Dizon replied. (There is none. Based on our investigation, there is none.)
According to DPWH Undersecretary Ricardo Bernabe III, the agency has so far listed 107 projects in Taguig, all of which have accomplishments.

"So I'll stop there. Mayroon na kayong... And everyone's open to look at it. The media, any investigating. Because I myself want to know kung may ghost. Kasi simula nu'ng nangyari itong flood control, tanong kami nang tanong sa sarili naming lugar. Kahit hindi ako taga-DPWH," Cayetano said.

(So I'll stop there. You have… And everyone's open to look at it. The media, any investigating. Because I myself want to know if there is a ghost. Ever since this flood control happened, we keep aksing if there are in our area, even if I am not from the DPWH.)
Cayetano has been embroiled in a verbal feud with Senator Ping Lacson after the two traded corruption allegations since July. Lacson has since then started a probe into Taguig projects.
Lacson said that his probe into Taguig City ghost projects opened a "cauldron of worms" upon meeting with officials from the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA). — VDV, GMA News

articles.summary: House prosecution panel spokesperson Rep. Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said Saturday that claims that Vice President Saa Duterte received suitcases containing billions of pesos “have to be taken…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 1:43pm

House prosecution panel spokesperson Rep. Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said Saturday that claims that Vice President Saa Duterte received suitcases containing billions of pesos “have to be taken seriously.”

"These allegations should be taken seriously. Kasi nagpakita siya... I think anyone who comes out with that serious and grave allegations should be taken seriously, and I think the NBI is taking cognizance of this," Adiong said in Bea Pinlac's report.

On Friday, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte as ordered by former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Gracioso supposedly served as a security officer for Velasco.
The new allegations, according to Adiong, could also be related to VP Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth, which is among the articles of impeachment.

“It’s not entirely connected with the articles of impeachment… I do not think it would directly impact the ongoing impeachment trial, but what I can tell you is that this is something that erodes the reputation of those mentioned... Separate po ‘yung impeachment trial,” he added.
The NBI has said that it is investigating Gracioso's claims.
GMA News has sought comments through phone calls and messages from Pulong Duterte, Rodrigo Duterte, and Velasco since Thursday, but they have yet to give any.
Sara denies
Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday has issued a statement saying she does not know Gracioso
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.

"This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case. The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," she said.
"The people want Marcos to take a public drug test. The people want Marcos to answer for the flood control scandal. The people want change," Duterte said. —with reports from Bea Pinlac/ VAL, GMA News

articles.title: White House bars CNN from travelling with Trump on Air Force One
articles.summary: CNN was scheduled to fly with US President Donald Trump for his trip to Tennessee on Saturday.

blocks.text: US broadcaster CNN has been barred from travelling with President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee on Saturday.
The move is the latest in a battle between the White House and the media after it was forced to lift its ban on some news outlets.

CNN was scheduled to fly with Trump for his trip to Tennessee for a college American football game until a note released on Friday night by the White House did not list the broadcaster on the media schedule.
The BBC has requested comment from the White House.
CNN has reported that no other outlet was listed as replacing them in the president's tentative schedule.
Last week Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists from the White House after accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
All three media outlets said they were pursuing legal action, and accused Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.

Four television networks that have a daily rotation of White House coverage along with CNN - ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC - had paused their broadcasts of the president in solidarity with the banned outlets.
The White House then launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, ahead of the United General Assembly in New York.
A federal judge has since ruled Trump barring news outlets from the White House was likely unconstitutional and the administration had to let them back in, at least for now.
However, the White House still denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday.

A White House communications account earlier posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call".
Regular US television coverage resumed on Friday after White House officials allowed reporters entry.
The president is set to attend a football game between University of Tennessee vs University of Texas College at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville from midday on Saturday.

articles.title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests
articles.summary:
New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices

Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people…

blocks.text: Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.

In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.
One important factor that can affect survival is how rapidly victims get access to treatment – every minute without CPR and defibrillation reduces the chance of survival by 10%.

“We have an objective as EMS [emergency medical service] organisations and EMS physicians to help cardiac arrest patients get defibrillated as early as possible,” said Matthieu Heidet, a professor of emergency medicine at Henri-Mondor university hospital in Créteil, France.
Work by Heidet and colleagues has suggested drones could be used to increase access to the life-saving devices.

To explore the issue, the team analysed the number and location of 28,349 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests that occurred between 2011 and 2024 in administrative areas within the Greater Paris area. Central Paris was excluded from the analysis.
The team cross-referenced these events with the location of fixed automated external defibrillators (AEDs).
The researchers found accessibility of the 1,893 AEDs varied considerably across the area.

“Only 30% of all [out-of-hospital cardiac arrest] cases occurred within the target 500-metre network distance of the nearest recorded fixed AED,” said Dr Hillary Minka, an emergency physician at the Lariboisière hospital in Paris and the first author of the work.

The team found an extra 910 fixed AEDs would be needed for 84.5% of the recorded cardiac arrest cases to have been within 500 metres of an AED, while 1,712 extra fixed AEDs would be needed for 100% coverage.
However, by using drones operating within a radius of 3,900 metres, coverage could be increased with fewer devices.

“As drone bases were introduced, the number of additional fixed AEDs required fell substantially,” said Minka, noting that with 100 drone bases and 26 additional fixed AEDs, more than 97% of the cardiac arrest cases would have been located either within 500 metres of a fixed AED or within approximately 4km (2.5 miles) of a drone base. The use of 200 drone bases and just four extra AEDs meant more than 99% of cases would have been covered.
The researchers also looked at the proportion of the cardiac arrest cases deemed close enough to an existing fixed AED that the device could be retrieved in a round trip within five minutes.
The results revealed only 30-40% of the cardiac arrest cases had access to current fixed AEDs within this time period using the ground transportation network.

Heidet added that this figure was optimistic. “In France, only 8% of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients benefit from the application of a public AED before the arrival of the [emergency services],” he said, noting one factor is that a large proportion of AEDs are inaccessible, for example because they are housed in enclosed private spaces that are not open at all times.
after newsletter promotion

By contrast, Minka noted that in a scenario involving 200 drone bases, 871 existing fixed AED sites and four additional fixed AED sites, drone delivery reached virtually all of the cardiac arrest cases covered by the model within five minutes.

The team’s models were based on drones being housed at sites ranging from current AED locations to fire stations and mobile intensive care units, and did not look at real-world deployment of such tech.
Heidet noted it is not the first time drones have been considered for the delivery of AEDs; the approach is already being used in parts of Sweden and has saved lives.
In real-world systems, Heidet added, drones are operated by trained drone pilots.

“Once an emergency call is received and an [out-of-hospital cardiac arrest] is identified at the dispatch centre, the drone is activated by EMS dispatchers. It then takes off and follows an automated flight path, while the final approach and subsequent AED delivery are handled by the drone pilot. The entire process is conducted under the supervision of the emergency medical service,” he said. Once delivered, the AED can be used by members of the public at the scene.
Heidet added the cost of drones needed to be integrated into the evaluation of such technology, noting there may be a balance between the ideal model and the feasible economic model.
The study, which has not yet been peer-reviewed, is to be presented at the European Emergency Medicine Congress in Paris on Saturday.

articles.title: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
articles.summary: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".

blocks.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has announced a ban on online gambling, just days before an election in which he is seeking a fourth term as the country's leader.
Lula, who is running against the son of the incarcerated former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, signed a provisional order on Friday that "prohibits all sports betting and online casinos".
The online gambling industry in Brazil was legalised in 2018 and has since been blamed for widespread household income losses due to addiction.
Lula described the industry as a "cancer" in his announcement, adding "either we remove the tumour, or it kills us".
The move comes just over a week before the first round of voting in Brazil's presidential election. Recent polls have the 80-year-old leader almost neck-and-neck with Flávio Bolsonaro.
The new measures must receive congressional approval within 120 days to remain in force.
Lula acknowledged online betting was created under the former President Michel Temer's administration but that it "grew without regulation under Bolsonaro's management", in a statement on X .
He said that there were "no restrictions" particularly for preventing children and adolescents from accessing online betting.
"We won't allow betting companies to profit at the expense of Brazilian families' income and lives," the president added.
The president described how he had heard from families who had sold everything in their houses because of their gambling addictions.
Separate to the online betting order, Lula also signed a bill to penalise criminal offences related to fixed-odds betting.
Earlier this week, at the United Nations General Assembly, Lula accused the industry of "transforming addiction into profit".
But Flávio Bolsonaro called the gambling crackdown "populist, hypocritical and politically motivated" during a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro on Friday, according to Reuters.
Most types of gambling, such as casinos and slot machines, are illegal in Brazil, but ever since online betting was legalised in 2018, it has exploded in popularity.
About 59.9% of Brazilian adults support banning internet betting, a survey by Atlas and Bloomberg published this week has found.

articles.title: TikTok agrees to settle with Alabama state over teen safety
articles.summary: The settlement involves TikTok adding several child safety measures to its platform including time limits and increased parental control. It is similar to a recent settlement competitor Meta had…

image.caption: TikTok has agreed to stricter access measures for teens, in what Alabama state has hailed as a 'landmark settlement'Image: Rüdiger Wölk/IMAGO

blocks.text: Short-form content sharing platform TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance reached a settlement with Alabama, the southeastern US state said on Friday, days ahead of what would have been a revealing trial over teen safety and its impact on their mental health.

As part of the deal, TikTok agreed to pay $100 million (€87.7 million) to the state of Alabama and enact measures for teens including a two-hour daily use limit, restricted access for children and pauses after 15 minutes of use.
However, the payout could rise to $300 million if 40 other states sign similar agreements with the company within a stipulated time period, the document said.
What have TikTok and Alabama state said after the settlement?
"This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually ​enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens," a spokesperson for TikTok's US operations said in a statement.
Meta settles for $18B. What it means for you.
Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall sued the social media giant last year.

At least 27 other states and Washington DC have brought similar lawsuits. Apart from these, TikTok faces thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts and municipalities over its impact on teen mental health. Meta Platforms, Snap Inc and Alphabet's YouTube are also defendants in many of these ​cases.

"This is a great day for Alabama parents. Tonight, they can rest easier knowing real protections are in place to shield their children from the dangers of social media addiction. TikTok has agreed to give parents real control over what their kids see and how much time they spend on the app," Marshall said in a press release.
With this, the company has settled all cases selected for trial against it, including claims by five young people and a Kentucky school district.
What were the allegations against TikTok?

The state of Alabama had argued that TikTok's endless stream of videos makes it the most addictive of social media platforms and that its algorithm specifically pushes young users toward content about violence and self harm.
The state held the app partially responsible for a teen mental health crisis and a significant increase in emergency room visits.
The lawsuit also accused TikTok of falsely claiming that it limits access to sexual and violent content for young users to have the app rated as 'safe for teens' on app stores.
It said that TikTok asks users to self-report their ages but also allows them to evade questions by viewing videos without creating an account.
That still earns the company data on viewing habits. Being able to scroll videos without signing in makes 'Kids Mode' an entirely useless feature, the lawsuit said.
France debates social media ban for teenagers
What measures will TikTok take?
As per the settlement, TikTok has to implement a series of safety measures, including:

items: Two-hour daily limit
Additional parental control limiting time on platform
'Productive pauses' interrupting continuous scrolling after 15 minutes, 60 minutes and 90 minutes
Restrict children access from 12 a.m. to 6 a.m.
Restrictions on push notifications during night and school hours
Robust measures to verify user age
Limits on discoverability of teen accounts by adults
Sending parents notifications of suspicious interactions between teen users and adults
Blanket ban on use of cosmetic filters by teens
Non-personalized feed for teens

blocks.text: Last month, Meta agreed to pay a massive $17 billion to 47 US states and territories in a similar case while agreeing to make changes to teens' access to its platforms, Facebook and Instagram.
It did not admit wrongdoing and conditioned $5 billion of the payout on TikTok, Snap and YouTube's adoption of the same terms. TikTok has not commented publicly about that deal.

articles.title: British climber, 28, dies in fall in northern Spain
articles.summary:
Mountaineer’s body recovered about 20 metres below the summit of Torrecerredo, the highest peak of the Picos de Europa range

A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft)…

blocks.text: A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft) while descending from the summit of a mountain in northern Spain, according to local law enforcement.

The 28-year-old mountaineer fell down a vertical gully on the east side of the Torrecerredo – the highest peak of the Cantabrian mountains – on Thursday afternoon, the Spanish Civil Guard for the Asturias region said.
The mountaineer’s remains were located after a rescue team aboard a helicopter flew over the area, the Civil Guard said.
Two specialists were lowered to retrieve the man’s body and his belongings which had been scattered during the fall.
The incident occurred during the descent, about 20 metres below the Torrecerredo peak, the Civil Guard said.
The mountaineer’s body was transported to La Morgal, a regional sports and aviation facility in Llanera near the Asturian city of Gijon.
A spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office said it had contacted local authorities about the death.
Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,649 metres, is the highest peak of the Picos de Europa mountain range, which is part of the larger Cantabrian Mountains range.

articles.title: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
articles.summary: Exploring the issues behind the escalation of tensions between the TPLF and the national army.

blocks.text: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
Image source, Reuters
Tigrayan forces have been patrolling the streets of Tigray's capital, Mekelle, this week
ByLucy Fleming and BBC Africa
Fighting has erupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray between regional forces and the national army.
Tigray residents, who have been trying to recover from a brutal two-year war that ended in 2022, fear a return to full-scale conflict.
There are reports of panic buying - and now internet and call services have been disrupted.
This means people cannot get access to their money via digital apps in what has become a largely cashless society after ATMs stopped working several months ago.
Why has fighting broken out now?
It follows more than six months of worsening relations between the government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that runs Tigray.

The African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides, ending the war nearly four years ago - but several issues have remained unresolved that have inflamed tensions.
This year, both sides have been trading blame while troops have mobilised amid pockets of fighting.
This week, major clashes erupted in Tigray and quickly spread into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. The two sides disagree over who started the latest escalation.
The TPLF says it was responding to a federal offensive, including drone strikes, while the government says Tigrayan forces attacked first after seizing control of airports in Tigray.
For much of Tigray's modern political history, it has been governed by the TPLF, which first emerged as an armed movement in the 1970s fighting Ethiopia's military government.

It became a major force in the overthrow of the Marxist regime in 1991 and went on to become the most powerful component of the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), the coalition that governed the ethnically diverse country for nearly three decades.
At times this proved contentious as some felt the TPLF held too much sway as Tigrayans only make up around 6% of Ethiopia's population.
When Abiy Ahmed became prime minister in 2018, he replaced the EPRDF with the Prosperity Party, significantly watering down the TPLF's influence.
Relations between Addis Ababa and the TPLF rapidly deteriorated until war erupted in 2020 in what was one of the most deadly conflicts this century.
The AU mediator estimated some 600,000 people died during the war, which totally cut off Tigray from the outside world and drove the region to the precipice of famine.
An uneasy truce was agreed in November 2022.
Why has the peace deal faltered?
There are four key issues - and two concern the fertile area of western Tigray.
The TPLF lost control of this territory in the early days of the war to Amhara, a region which neighbours Tigray to the west and whose fighters had fought on the side of the Ethiopian army.
Many people in Amhara believe the territory of western Tigray should never have been incorporated into Tigray when regional boundaries were redrawn after the military regime was ousted in 1991.
When its fighters seized control during the recent civil war, hundreds of thousands of ethnic Tigrayan people fled and are now living in homeless camps in Tigray and in the capital, Addis Ababa.
The TPLF wants western Tigray back and for those displaced from the territory to return. The government says the future of the territory needs to be decided by a referendum.

blocks.caption: Image caption, People have been reportedly rushing to buy food, panicking that a full-blown war will start

blocks.text: People have been reportedly rushing to buy food, panicking that a full-blown war will start
For the government, a major matter of contention has been disarmament. It says the TPLF has only handed over old weaponry to the AU and has been hiding its arms.
The two sides have also been at loggerheads over how Tigray should be governed. Under the terms of the deal, an interim administration was appointed by Abiy.

But attempts by the prime minister to influence affairs caused disputes within the TPLF itself and just before the general election in May, which was not held in Tigray because of the security situation, it restored its pre-war administration, disbanding the one set up by Abiy.
This has meant that civil servants are longer being paid and other services have been seizing up, worsening economic conditions.
Who is backing the TPLF?
A major development has seen the TPLF, once politically isolated inside Ethiopia, gain several key allies.

Earlier in September, it joined six other armed movements in forming what is called the Alliance for Survival, which includes those actively fighting the government like Amhara's Fano militia and the Oromo Liberation Army.
Members of the new alliance have different grievances, but they do share one objective: they want to remove Abiy's government from power.

blocks.caption: BBC map of Ethiopia showing the northern states of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. The regional capital of Mekelle is labelled in Tigray and the national capital Addis Ababa is also located near the centre of the country and just outside the three northern states. Eritrea is shown to the north, borderin…

blocks.text: So while the TPLF and Fano forces were on opposite sides during the civil war - and still disagree over the fate of western Tigray - they have temporarily put some of their differences aside.
TPLF officials say they do not want to repeat the situation of 2020, when they felt surrounded and isolated.
Yet analysts caution the alliance may become difficult to maintain because its members ultimately have very different interests.
What is the government's position?
As well as blaming the TPLF for starting the recent fighting, it has criticised the new alliance, portraying it as an attempt to destabilise the country.
It has also accused Eritrea of supporting armed groups inside Ethiopia, something Asmara denies.
During the recent civil war, Eritrea fought alongside Ethiopian troops but the two neighbours, which have long had a volatile relationship, have again fallen out.
Their disagreement centres on the Red Sea and its ports.

Ethiopia, the world's most populous landlocked nation, lost access to them when Eritrea seceded in 1993. Recently Prime Minister Abiy has been pushing for ownership of Eritrea's southern port of Assab - about 60km (37 miles) from the border - and hinted at taking it by force.
What do we know about the bombing in Tigray?
Reports indicate that federal forces have been using drones and other military operations against Tigrayan forces.

The government's stated justification is that it is responding to attacks and trying to defend federal positions and territory. However, the circumstances surrounding individual strikes are difficult to independently verify.
Residents in one recently targeted town told the BBC the drones had hit two schools, which local officials said had been used by Ethiopian troops as military bases during the war.
This suggests Addis Ababa may believe they are again being used for a military purpose - by Tigrayan forces.
The attacks have come amid reports that the TPLF has been forcibly recruiting young men to join its ranks.
What is being done to stop the fighting?
The main diplomatic effort is being led by the AU, which has called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to direct talks.
It has asked former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, the AU's special Horn of Africa envoy, to engage the parties urgently.
The UN has made a similar appeal, warning against a wider and more devastating conflict.
The regional organisation Igad has also called for fighting to stop and dialogue to resume.
The difficulty is that trust between Addis Ababa and Tigray is extremely low, while the formation of the new armed alliance has made the situation more complicated.
Could the fighting spread?
Tigray capital "out of cash" as fighting escalates
Yes, there is a significant risk of wider conflict inside Ethiopia.
The fighting has already moved to areas over and along Tigray's borders, while the government is simultaneously dealing with armed conflicts in other regions, particularly Amhara and Oromia.
The new alliance potentially connects several of these conflicts politically and militarily.
There is also a fear that Eritrea could be drawn in again - this time against the government.
The two aggressors in Sudan's civil war are also on opposite sides when it comes to allegiances in Tigray, potentially complicating matters.
The AU has specifically urged all neighbouring countries not to take actions that could further escalate the crisis.
